q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
Let me work through this systematically.

## (a) Time left until resolution

Today is 2026-08-21. NVIDIA is set to report Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. That's **5 days** until the earnings release and the guidance announcement.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** (prospective guidance for future quarters) in the Q2 FY2027 earnings release, specifically the revenue figure.

Based on the research provided:
- NVIDIA issued guidance on May 20, 2026 for Q2 FY2027 of $91.0 billion ± 2% ($89.2B to $92.8B range)
- Wall Street consensus as of mid-August 2026 averages $91.85-$91.9 billion
- Q1 FY2027 actual was $81.6 billion, beating guidance by ~$2 billion
- The research explicitly notes that "The crucial figure to watch in the upcoming release will be NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q3 FY2027, which analysts currently peg at $103.1 billion"

The question appears to be asking what NVIDIA will **guide for Q3 FY2027** (the next quarter after the one being reported), not the Q2 guidance that was already issued in May.

Current analyst consensus for Q3 FY2027 guidance is $103.1 billion, per the research.

Given:
- NVIDIA's strong execution trend (beating Q1 by ~$2.4%)
- The $103.1 billion analyst consensus for Q3 FY2027
- The strong growth trajectory implied (from $81.6B actual Q1 to ~$91B expected Q2 guidance to $103.1B expected Q3 guidance)
- NVIDIA's typical practice of providing realistic guidance given track record
- The range provided (99.5B to 115.5B) brackets the current analyst consensus

The most likely outcome is that NVIDIA will guide to approximately **$103-104 billion** for Q3 FY2027 revenue, slightly above current consensus given their pattern of beating guidance.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Significant deterioration in data center demand or AI momentum
- Unexpected supply chain disruptions
- Weakness in international markets or additional geopolitical constraints on China sales
- Conservative guidance shift (though NVIDIA has beaten guidance recently)
- Macro slowdown affecting customer capital expenditure plans

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Continued strong demand for AI infrastructure and accelerators
- Better-than-expected bookings and forward orders
- Upside from enterprise and cloud customers deploying more aggressively than anticipated
- Continued market share gains or ASP expansion
- Following the pattern of beating prior guidance by 2-3%

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

The research provides:
- Q1 FY2027 actual: $81.6 billion (beat guidance by ~$2B or ~2.4%)
- Q2 FY2027 guidance: $91.0B ± 2% (range $89.2-92.8B)
- Q3 FY2027 analyst consensus: $103.1 billion
- Current range provided: 99.5B to 115.5B

Historical pattern shows NVIDIA beats guidance by modest amounts (1-3%), suggesting Q3 guidance would likely be set slightly conservatively relative to current consensus.

---

**Reasoning to probability distribution:**

The analyst consensus of $103.1 billion appears well-grounded and sits near the midpoint of the provided range (99.5-115.5). Given:
- 5 days to resolution (minimal new information likely)
- NVIDIA's recent track record of beating guidance
- The tight clustering of analyst estimates
- The narrowing timeframe means the consensus view is essentially "locked in"

The most probable outcome is guidance in the $102-105 billion range, with slightly lower probability of values below $100B (would require significant deterioration) or above $110B (would require major positive surprise).

I estimate the distribution as:
- 10th percentile: ~100.5B (slight downside tail risk)
- 50th percentile: ~103.5B (consensus + modest beat pattern)
- 90th percentile: ~107.5B (upside from strong execution)

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to report its Q2 FY2027 earnings on Wednesday, August 26, 2026. The company's own guidance, issued on May 20, 2026, projects Q2 FY2027 revenue to be $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [investor.nvidia.com](https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Financial-Results-for-First-Quarter-Fiscal-2027/), [sec.gov](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000051/q1fy27pr.htm). This guidance explicitly excludes any Data Center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, as of August 19, 2026, have an average estimate for Q2 FY2027 revenue at $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/), with some consensus figures from August 12, 2026, placing it at $91.85 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/). This analyst consensus falls within NVIDIA's own guided range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). For the previous quarter (Q1 FY2027), NVIDIA reported $81.6 billion in revenue, exceeding its guidance by approximately $2 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

The crucial figure to watch in the upcoming release will be NVIDIA's forward guidance for Q3 FY2027, which analysts currently peg at $103.1 billion [rexshares.com](https://www.rexshares.com/nvidia-earnings/).
